decisions.reason: Correctly grounds the diagnosis in the session log and env-state: the session/tool worker runs inside the host process whose tree npm is replacing, the host dies mid-install, the GUI disconnects, and the tool call's outcome remains unknown. Explicitly frames it as structural, not flaky/network.

Explains that package content persists while dsh/dsh.cmd shims are missing and dsh.ps1 is stale, so content presence does not equal a working install, and explicitly rejects hand-swapping directories or hand-written shims as worse, tying it to the nonstandard tree in env-state.txt.

Describes the recorded repair: rerunning the pinned npm install -g from an external shell so npm regenerates all shims, verifying dsh --version is rc.1, and aligning the reference source checkout to the same tag. Presented as the documented repair/verification, not as actions the candidate executed.

The agent recognizes it runs on the upgrade target, refuses to execute the global install, and hands off an ordered external procedure: fully stop the host, run the exact-version pinned install externally, then restart, hard-refresh, and verify. Correctly attributes stop-host-first and pinning to established rules and the never-from-inside rule as new.

Proposes a guard relating the requested upgrade target to the session's own runtime path in the global dsh tree, uses the repair notes' alpha.5-to-rc.1 version-only diff to conclude no plugin re-migration is needed, and covers version markers, plugin loading after refresh, and optional backup cleanup only after verification.

caps.reason: The report's final advice is to refuse in-session execution and hand off an external stop-then-install procedure; it never recommends running the upgrade from inside the live host.
Manual directory swaps and handmade shims are explicitly rejected in favor of the formal external pinned installation.
